ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a horizontally placed parallel-plate capacitor, the upper plate is marked -Q, and the lower plate is marked +Q; the left half between the two plates is drawn with diagonal hatching, indicating dielectric, and the right half is an air region; the positively charged particle +q is located in the right-side air region and is marked with mass m. Then reason: Since the lower plate is positive and the upper plate is negative, the electric field direction is from the positive plate toward the negative plate, so the electric field in the air gap is vertically upward. Initially the particle is positively charged, so the electric field force qE_i is upward; the particle is in equilibrium, indicating qE_i=mg. Treat the left and right halves as two parallel-plate capacitors in parallel: one half is air, one half is dielectric, and the dielectric relative permittivity kappa>1. The initial total capacitance C_i=(epsilon0 A/2d)(1+kappa), and after removing the dielectric the total capacitance C_f=epsilon0 A/d. Because kappa>1, C_i>C_f. The total charge Q on the plates remains unchanged, V=Q/C, therefore after removing the dielectric the voltage increases, and the electric field between the plates E=V/d also increases, namely E_f>E_i. Thus after removing the dielectric qE_f>mg, and the net force is upward.

raw_record.question_text: A large parallel plate capacitor is placed horizontally, with half of the space between the plates filled with an isotropic uniform dielectric and the other half with air, as shown in the figure. When the two plates are charged with a constant equal but opposite charge, a particle with mass \(m\) and charge \(+q\) is in equilibrium in the air region between the plates. If the dielectric is then removed, in which direction will the particle move?

method.method_draft: First use the image to identify the field direction: bottom plate is +Q and top plate is −Q, so the electric field in the air gap points upward. Model the initial geometry as two parallel capacitors of equal area, one air and one dielectric. Because the total plate charge is fixed and κ>1, removing the dielectric lowers the capacitance, so the voltage and field between the plates increase. Initially the particle is in equilibrium, so qE_i=mg. After removal E_f>E_i, hence qE_f>mg and the net force is upward. Therefore the particle moves upward.
